sections.sourcing: No F&F-specific sourcing moves this week, but the backdrop for its main supply base is strong: Bangladesh's garment exports rose 8.8% year on year to $3.08bn in September 2026. Shipments to the UK were $915.6m in July–August of FY27, up from $882.6m a year earlier. Bangladesh remains the largest supplier to the UK by volume, which supports F&F's reliance on Dhaka-based knit and sweater mills.
sections.strategy: On 28 September Tesco started a one-store trial of AIUTA's AI virtual try-on at its Sandhurst Extra. Shoppers can try on about 1,500 F&F womenswear and menswear items by uploading a photo to an in-store screen. This adds to the September relaunch of F&F online (web and app). Investors will look for clothing commentary in the H1 2026/27 interim results on 8 October, after F&F grew 5.1% to more than £1.2bn in FY25/26.
sections.pricing: The F&F autumn promotion ended on 4 October. Key AW items were priced at £16 (stirrup leggings), £22.50 (pencil midi skirt), £45 (faux suede funnel-neck jacket) and £55 (faux fur aviator jacket). That keeps F&F above Sainsbury's Tu, which has basics from £5, denim at £20 and hero outerwear under £40, and clearly above Primark on entry price.
sections.launches: F&F's AW26 online range is still being rolled out after 400 new styles, extra sizes and online-only ranges launched on 17 September. Tesco has said more styles are 'launching soon'. We found no separate collection drop dated this week.
sections.gossip: Most of the industry focus is on Thursday's interim results (8 October). An IG preview frames the question as whether Tesco can protect its market share gains while absorbing higher costs. F&F's online relaunch and the virtual try-on pilot are seen as Tesco challenging George's renewed push in clothing, though Tesco has not confirmed a wider try-on rollout.
soWhat: F&F's online expansion (more styles, extended sizes, online-only ranges) points to more SKUs in smaller, faster-turning orders. Suppliers should prepare to bid on short-run online-exclusive capsules and expect more demand for extended sizing.

Virtual try-on relies on accurate digital garment assets. Vendors that can supply clean product imagery or 3D/digital twins with each style will be easier for Tesco to onboard as the pilot grows, which is a direct opportunity for Textile3D-type capability.
Watch the 8 October interims. If clothing like-for-like sales come in strong, expect bigger SS27 buys and a fight for Bangladesh knit capacity, so lock in mill slots before Q4 negotiations.
